title: Universal first order thickenings and conormal sheaves restrict to open subschemes
statement: Let $h:Z\to X$ be a formally unramified morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism] and $Z\subset Z'$ a universal first order thickening of $Z$ over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]. Let $V\subset Z$ and $U\subset X$ be open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion] with $h(V)\subset U$, and let $V'\subset Z'$ be the open subscheme with $V=Z\cap V'$ (it has the same underlying set as $V$, since $Z$ and $Z'$ have the same underlying space). Then $h|_V:V\to U$ is formally unramified, $V\subset V'$ (with $V'\to U$ the restriction of $Z'\to X$) is a universal first order thickening of $V$ over $U$, and consequently $\mathcal C_{Z/X}|_V\cong\mathcal C_{V/U}$ [def-weil-pbc-conormal-sheaf-formally-unramified].

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 04FA (lemma-universal-thickening-localize), with Lemma 02HC (lemma-formally-unramified-on-opens) for the first assertion

proof.text: *$h|_V$ is formally unramified.* Write $j_V:V\to Z$, $j_U:U\to X$ for the inclusions and $h|_V:V\to U$ for the unique morphism with $j_U\circ h|_V=h\circ j_V$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. Since $h$ is formally unramified and $h(V)\subseteq U$, $h|_V$ is formally unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-open-restriction] (Stacks 02HC: two $U$-morphisms $T'\to V$ extending the same $T\to V$ give, after composing with $j_V$, two $X$-morphisms $T'\to Z$ extending the same $T\to Z$, which agree since $h$ is formally unramified, so they agree because $j_V$ is a monomorphism).

source.place: Lemma 04FA (lemma-universal-thickening-localize), proof, first sentence: 'The first statement is Lemma 02HC'

proof.text: *$V\subset V'$ is a first order thickening over $U$.* Let $i_Z:Z\to Z'$ be the closed immersion and $h':Z'\to X$ the structure morphism, $h'\circ i_Z=h$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]. A first order thickening is a thickening, so $i_Z$ is a homeomorphism of $Z$ onto $Z'$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]; hence $V'=i_Z(V)$ is open in $Z'$ and $V=i_Z^{-1}(V')$, i.e. $V'$ exists and $V=Z\cap V'$. Every point of $V'$ is $i_Z(v)$ with $v\in V$, and $h'(i_Z(v))=h(v)\in U$; so $h'(V')\subseteq U$ and there is a unique $h'_{V'}:V'\to U$ with $j_U\circ h'_{V'}=h'\circ j_{V'}$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-open-restriction] (applied to $i_Z$, $V'$ and $X\supseteq U$), the restriction $i_V:V\to V'$, the unique morphism with $j_{V'}\circ i_V=i_Z\circ j_V$, is a closed immersion whose ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_V$ is the restriction $\mathcal I|_{V'}$ of the ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ of $i_Z$, $\mathcal I_V^2=0$, and $V\subset V'$ is a first order thickening over $U$ through $h'_{V'}$. It is compatible with $h|_V$: $j_U\circ h'_{V'}\circ i_V=h'\circ i_Z\circ j_V=h\circ j_V=j_U\circ h|_V$, so $h'_{V'}\circ i_V=h|_V$ by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme].

source.place: Proof of Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), first paragraph ('general remarks'): 'Let V' \subset Z' be the open subscheme such that V = Z \cap V''; Definition 04EX (definition-thickening); Lemma 09ZU (lemma-base-change-thickening)

proof.text: *Existence of the dotted arrow.* Let $T\subset T'$ be a first order thickening over $U$, with closed immersion $i_T:T\to T'$ and structure morphism $b:T'\to U$, and let $a:T\to V$ with $h|_V\circ a=b\circ i_T$. Then $T\subset T'$ is a first order thickening over $X$ through $j_U\circ b$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], and $a_Z:=j_V\circ a:T\to Z$ satisfies $h\circ a_Z=j_U\circ h|_V\circ a=(j_U\circ b)\circ i_T$. By the universal property of $Z'$ over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening] there is a unique $a'':T'\to Z'$ with $h'\circ a''=j_U\circ b$ and $a''\circ i_T=i_Z\circ j_V\circ a$. Since $T\subset T'$ is a thickening, $i_T$ is surjective on underlying spaces [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], so every point of $T'$ is $i_T(t)$ and $a''(i_T(t))=i_Z(j_V(a(t)))\in i_Z(V)=V'$; hence $a''(T')\subseteq V'$ and there is a unique $a':T'\to V'$ with $j_{V'}\circ a'=a''$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. It is a morphism of thickenings over $U$: $j_U\circ h'_{V'}\circ a'=h'\circ j_{V'}\circ a'=h'\circ a''=j_U\circ b$, so $h'_{V'}\circ a'=b$; and $j_{V'}\circ a'\circ i_T=a''\circ i_T=i_Z\circ j_V\circ a=j_{V'}\circ i_V\circ a$, so $a'\circ i_T=i_V\circ a$; both by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] ($j_U$, $j_{V'}$ are monomorphisms).

source.place: Proof of Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), first paragraph: 'By the universal property of Z' we obtain (a, a'). But since we have equality |T| = |T'| of underlying topological spaces we see that a'(T') \subset V'. Hence we may think of (a, a') as a morphism of thickenings (T \subset T') \to (V \subset V') over U'

proof.text: *Uniqueness of the dotted arrow; conclusion.* If $a'_1,a'_2:T'\to V'$ both satisfy $h'_{V'}\circ a'_k=b$ and $a'_k\circ i_T=i_V\circ a$, then $j_{V'}\circ a'_k:T'\to Z'$ satisfies $h'\circ j_{V'}\circ a'_k=j_U\circ h'_{V'}\circ a'_k=j_U\circ b$ and $j_{V'}\circ a'_k\circ i_T=j_{V'}\circ i_V\circ a=i_Z\circ j_V\circ a$, so $j_{V'}\circ a'_1=j_{V'}\circ a'_2$ by the uniqueness in the universal property of $Z'$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening], and $a'_1=a'_2$ by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. With Steps 2 and 3, $V\subset V'$ (with $h'_{V'}$) is a universal first order thickening of $V$ over $U$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening].

source.place: Proof of Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), first paragraph: 'Uniqueness is clear also'

proof.text: *Conormal sheaves.* By [def-weil-pbc-conormal-sheaf-formally-unramified] the conormal sheaf $\mathcal C_{V/U}$ may be computed in the universal first order thickening $V\subset V'$ of Steps 2-4 (any other choice is isomorphic to it by a unique isomorphism over $U$ compatible with $V$, by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening-exists]): $\mathcal C_{V/U}=i_V^*\mathcal I_V$, while $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=i_Z^*\mathcal I$. The restriction to the open subscheme $V$ is the pullback along $j_V$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction], and pullbacks compose, $(g\circ f)^*\cong f^*g^*$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Hence, using $i_Z\circ j_V=j_{V'}\circ i_V$ and $\mathcal I|_{V'}=\mathcal I_V$ (Step 2, [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-open-restriction] (2)): $\mathcal C_{Z/X}|_V\cong j_V^*i_Z^*\mathcal I\cong(i_Z\circ j_V)^*\mathcal I=(j_{V'}\circ i_V)^*\mathcal I\cong i_V^*j_{V'}^*\mathcal I\cong i_V^*(\mathcal I|_{V'})=i_V^*\mathcal I_V=\mathcal C_{V/U}$.
